task: Audit log queries are slow because the audit table is rebuilt nightly from application logs. Keep a full history of changes as they happen.

candidate_memories.content: The audit system uses event sourcing: every state change is appended as an immutable event to audit_events; the current state is derived by replaying the event stream.
Event sourcing provides a complete, immutable history of all state changes without nightly rebuilds; queries against event streams are faster than rebuilding from logs.
audit_events table is append-only with a composite index on (entity_type, entity_id, occurred_at); queries by entity_id are O(log n).
Audit logs are also shipped to Splunk for SIEM analysis; Splunk ingestion is separate from the event-sourced audit_events table.
candidate_memories.notes: note: Splunk is a separate log sink, not the event sourcing system

candidate_memories.content: Database change-data-capture (CDC) captures row-level changes but requires the source table to exist; CDC is not the same as event sourcing.
candidate_memories.notes: note: CDC is a different history mechanism

candidate_memories.content: Nightly rebuild job takes 4 h and is the primary source of slow audit queries; event sourcing eliminates the need for the rebuild.
